mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (< -0.3) between GDPC1 YoY decline and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which elevates wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (< -0.3) between INDPRO decline and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over the same month signals housing market overbuilding coinciding with weakening overall demand, which increases credit risk and reduces consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL over two months signals a tightening monetary policy with falling inflation, which typically supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month AND CPIAUCSL < previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above trend by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% in a single month signals a surge in consumer savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumption and weaker corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average + 10% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.
